answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded reputation with a slow inlet: each agent locks a refundable bond before transacting, and trust grows only through verified useful work over time, not by minting new identities. A sybil attacker can spawn many accounts, but each needs its own bond and its own history, so cost rises linearly while honest standing cannot be copied. Like a ripple from one verified entry, reputation spreads gradually; a comet-fast flood of fresh identities is throttled at the inlet until bonds and work prove it real.
